title: An improved protocol for generation and characterization of human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived retinal pigment epithelium cells
protocol: Prepare ultra-low attachment plates by adding 1 mL of mTeSR plus medium to each well.
Aspirate the spent medium from the plate containing iPSCs, and rinse the plate once with CTS™ DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+).
Aspirate CTS™ DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+) and add ReLeSR Solution to the plate containing iPSCs.
Adjust the volume of ReLeSR Solution for various plate sizes.
Add 1 mL/well of ReLeSR™ and aspirate ReLeSR™ within 1 min, such that colonies are exposed to a thin film of liquid.
Incubate at 37°C for 4 min ± 30 s.
Add an appropriate amount of mTeSR plus to each plate to stop the dissociation reaction.
Gently pipet the dissociated cells up and down sufficiently to disperse the colonies into a single-cell suspension.
Transfer the iPSC suspension from each well into a separate 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the tube(s) at 200 g for 3 min to pellet the cells.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant from the iPSC pellet.
Resuspend the pellet with approximately 6 mL of mTeSR plus medium.
Add resuspended cells to each well of a 6-well ultra-low attachment plate containing 6 mL mTeSR plus medium (1 mL per well).
Add 10 μM ROCK inhibitor to each well.
Incubate the cells for 24 hours in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator to form EBs.
Replace the media with 2 mL of fresh mTeSR plus medium to remove Y-27632.
Gently swirl the EB plate and bring the EBs to the center of the dish on Day 1 and Day 2.
Remove 1 mL of medium from the well corner on Day 1 and Day 2.
Add 1 mL of fresh mTeSR plus medium to each well.
Gradually shift the medium of the suspension cultures with EBs from mTeSR plus to differentiation induction media (DIM).
Replace one part of mTeSR plus media with DIM on Day 3 in a 3:1 ratio.
Replace one part of mTeSR plus media with DIM on Day 4 in a 1:1 ratio.
Give complete media change with DIM on Day 5.
Matrigel coat and EB plate on Day 6.
Plate the EBs on Matrigel-coated culture dishes.
Gently swirl the EB plate to transfer EBs from 3 wells of a 6 well plate into a 15 mL tube.
Allow the EBs to settle at room temperature for about 3 minutes.
Remove supernatant, retaining 1 mL of media.
Add 2 mL of DIM and resuspend with 500 μL of retained media in a drop-wise manner.
Gently shake the culture plate to aid uniform distribution of aggregates.
Place the culture plate back in the incubator without disturbing it for 24 hours.
Observe plates after 24 hours for EB attachment.
Discard floating EBs while changing medium on Day 7-8.
Complete media change with 100% DIM on Day 7-8.
Prepare Differentiation Propagation Media (DPM) as shown in Table 3.
Add N1 supplement to filtered DPM media.
Store prepared DPM media at 4°C for up to 2 weeks.
Gradually shift medium from DIM to DPM by replacing one part of DIM with DPM on Day 9.
Give complete media change with 100% DPM on Day 10.
Feed cultures with DPM on alternate days until day 22.
Prepare RPEMM as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Add growth factors and supplements to filtered media for RPEMM.
Store prepared RPEMM at 4°C for up to 2 weeks.
Gradually switch the medium from DPM to Retinal Pigment Epithelium Maturation Media (RPEMM).
Replace one part of DPM with RPEMM on day 23 (1:1 ratio).
Switch completely to RPEMM on day 24.
Feed cultures with RPEMM on alternate days until day 40.
Aspirate the culture medium from RPE cells.
Wash cells once with CTS™ DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+) using 1 mL/well.
Incubate cells with pre-warmed GCDR and Accutase at a 1:1 ratio for 11–12 minutes at 37°C.
Pipette gently to dissociate cells into single cells or aggregates of 5–10 cells.
Dilute cell suspension with RPEMM media.
Collect cell suspension in a 15 mL tube and centrifuge at 200 g for 3 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in RPEMM media.
Seed cells 1:2 or 1:3 in matrigel-coated plates.
Allow cells to attach without disturbing for 24–48 hours.
Resume media change after proper cell attachment.
Feed cultures with RPEMM on alternate days until day 75-80.
OPTIONAL: Pass RPE cells around day 60 (±5) by following the steps mentioned in Enrichment step by passaging of RPE.
Maintain RPE cells up to day 90–100 by changing medium on alternate days if further scale-up is needed.
Select and cryopreserve RPE cells at Day 75 or later when they show cuboidal morphology with visible deposits of melanin pigment.
Wash the RPE cells twice with CTS™ DPBS (-Ca2+/-Mg2+).
Add pre-warmed GCDR and Accutase at a 1:1 ratio and incubate for 10–12 minutes at 37°C.
Manually remove any visibly non-pigmented cluster areas using pipette tips.
Gently flush the pigmenting patches out from the wells with pipette tips until all pigmented patches have been successfully detached.
Collect the cells and mix with equal volumes of RPEMM.
Centrifuge at 200 g for 2 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Count the cells and determine the number of cryovials required to freeze approximately 1 million cells per vial in 1 mL of cold freezing medium.
Label each cryovial with cell line name, cell type, initials, and date.
Add Cryostor CS10 freezing medium to the RPE cell pellet and gently mix the RPE cell suspension.
Place the cryovials containing 1 million cells per vial in a Mr. Frosty freezing container.
Store the cryovials at -80°C for 24 hours.
Transfer the cells from the Mr. Frosty freezing container to the liquid nitrogen storage tank after 24 hours.
Update the cryotank binder with relevant information about the stored cells.
Aspirate the culture medium.
Gently wash the cultures thrice with CTS-DPBS (-Ca2+/-Mg2+) solution.
Incubate for 15-20 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C) with fixing solution.
Remove the fixing solution and gently wash thrice with CTS-DPBS (-Ca2+/-Mg2+) solution.
Permeabilize and block by adding blocking solution.
Incubate the blocking solution for 30 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Gently wash thrice with CTS-DPBS (-Ca2+/-Mg2+) solution.
Add primary antibody diluted in antibody diluent.
Incubate overnight (16-20 hours) at 4°C.
Remove primary antibody and wash thrice with CTS-DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+).
Add secondary antibody diluted in antibody diluent and incubate in dark for 60 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Remove secondary antibody solution and wash thrice with CTS-DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+).
Counterstain with 1 μg/mL concentration of DAPI and incubate in dark for 10 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Remove DAPI solution and wash once with CTS-DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+).
Add CTS-DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+) (300 μL for 1 well of a 4 well plate) and visualize under a fluorescent microscope.
Aspirate culture media and wash cells with CTS-DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+).
Harvest cells enzymatically using GCDR and Accutase at a 1:1 ratio for 10–12 min.
Gently pipette to make a single cell suspension.
Centrifuge at 200 g for 3 min and discard the supernatant.
Wash the pellet by resuspending in CTS-DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+) and centrifuge at 200 g for 3 min.
Fix the cells by adding 1 mL of 4% PFA for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash the cells with CTS-DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+) and centrifuge at 200 g for 3 min.
Completely remove CTS-DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+).
Add 1 mL of ice-cold methanol to the pellet and incubate at 4°C for 20 min.
Wash cells with FACS buffer and centrifuge at 200 g for 3 min.
Stain the cells with primary antibody at an optimized concentration in 100 μL FACS buffer and incubate for 30 min at room temperature.
Repeat wash with FACS buffer and centrifuge at 200 g for 3 min.
Add secondary antibody in 100 μL FACS buffer to the pellet at optimized concentration and incubate in dark for 30 min.
Vortex the vials every 10 min to ensure mixing.
Wash with CTS-DPBS (1×) (-Ca2+/-Mg2+) and resuspend in FACS buffer.
Transfer the cells to flow tubes for flow cytometry analysis.
Collect cells in a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge for one minute at 200 g to pellet down the cells.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Snap freeze the cell pellet using liquid nitrogen.
Store snap-frozen cells at -80°C until RNA isolation.
Use the RNeasy Mini kit (Qiagen) for RNA isolation.
Add 500 μL of RLT buffer to the cell pellet.
Add an equal volume of 70% ethanol to the mixture.
Transfer the mixture into the spin column and spin at 8,000 g for one minute.
Wash the column once with Buffer RW1.
Wash the column twice with Buffer RPE.
Incubate a final elution step by adding 20 μL of RNAse-free water to the spin column.
Spin at 8,000 g for one minute to elute the RNA.
Keep the eluted RNA immediately on ice.
Quantify RNA using a nanodrop.
Perform all cDNA synthesis reaction setup steps on ice.
Prepare the cDNA synthesis reaction mix on ice according to the Verso cDNA synthesis kit protocol.
Incubate at 42°C for 45 minutes to allow cDNA synthesis.
Incubate at 95°C for 2 minutes to inactivate the enzyme.
Prepare a 20 μL reaction mixture containing 10 μL of SYBR green mix (2×), 1 μL each of forward and reverse primer (stock 10 μM), 2 μL of cDNA (50 ng), and 6 μL of water for qPCR using SYBR green.
Prepare a 20 μL reaction mixture containing 10 μL of Taqman master mix (2×), 1 μL of the gene-specific probe (stock 20×), 2 μL of cDNA (50 ng), and 7 μL of water for qPCR using Taqman probes.
Perform RT-qPCR experiments in minimal light.
Normalize gene expression levels against Beta-ACTIN/GAPDH as housekeeping genes.
Calculate fold change by normalizing sample expression (RPE) to a control (iPSC).
Coat the ELISA plate with 100 μL of capture antibody and incubate overnight at room temperature.
Wash coated wells with wash buffer three times.
Add 300 μL of reagent diluent as blocking solution and incubate for 1 hour.
Repeat washing three times with wash buffer.
Add 100 μL of the sample or standards diluted in reagent dilution to the coated wells and incubate for 2 hours.
Wash thrice with wash buffer carefully.
Add 100 μL of detection antibody diluted in reagent diluent and incubate for 2 minutes.
Wash thrice with wash buffer carefully.
Add 100 μL of Streptavidin-HRP to each well.
Cover the plate and incubate for 20 minutes in dark.
Add 100 μL of substrate solution and incubate for 20 min in the absence of direct light.
Add 50 μL of Stop Solution to each well.
Mix the plate gently after adding the Stop Solution.
Determine the optical density of each well immediately at 450 nm and 540 nm using Varioskan LUX microplate reader for background subtraction.
Breed a colony of Pigmented RCS (RCS-p+/Lav) rats from NIH Rat Resource and Research Center.
Feed animals with standard laboratory chow.
Maintain animals on a 12 h dark/light cycle.
Wean animals at postnatal day 21.
Administer oral cyclosporine A in drinking water.
Transfer cells to a 37°C water bath for 2 min for thawing from liquid nitrogen storage.
Add 1 ml of pre-warmed DMEM/F12 media dropwise to the vial after thawing.
Transfer cells to a 15 ml tube containing 5 ml of pre-warmed DMEM/F12 media.
Rinse cryotube with 1 mL of DMEM/F12 media and add to 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge cells at 150 g for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aspirate supernatant and re-suspend cells in 1 mL of pre-warmed DMEM/F12 media.
Pipette up and down to re-suspend the cells carefully.
Remove 10 μL of cell suspension and add to 10 μL of 0.08% Trypan blue solution.
Pipette up and down and load hemacytometer (10 μL each side).
Count viable cells.
Centrifuge cell suspension again at 150 g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in appropriate volume to achieve desired concentration for injection.
Dilate pupils with 1% tropicamide and 2.5% phenylephrine one hour before injections.
Anesthetize eyes with topical 0.5% proparacaine HCl.
Sedate animals with intraperitoneal ketamine/xylazine (100/10 mg/kg).
Cut the corner of the eyelid to allow for visualization of the posterior retina.
Use a hemostat to reduce blood accumulation.
Make a small scleral/choroidal incision (∼1 mm) 2-mm posterior to the limbus in the dorsotemporal region using 27 gauge needle tip.
Make a small lateral corneal puncture using a 30-G needle.
Deliver two microliters of cell suspension or control media into the subretinal space using a fine glass pipette connected to a Hamilton syringe via microtubing.
Score the subretinal bleb based on size and injection-related issues, such as bleeding, bubbles, cells in the vitreous.
Place 0.5% erythromycin ointment on eyes after surgery.
Administer intraperitoneal dexamethasone (1.0 mg/kg) on surgery day.
Administer dexamethasone every other day for 2 weeks post-cell transplantation to minimize potential inflammatory response.
Start animals on cyclosporine A one day prior to injections.
Prepare a virtual optomotor system (VOS) with four computer monitors arranged in a square.
Place the animal on the pedestal in the center of the monitors.
Allow the animal 5 minutes to acclimate to the pedestal.
Set up the simple staircase examination for both eyes using Cerebral Mechanics software, keeping the contrast at 100%.
Begin the examination with a low spatial frequency grating.
Incrementally increase the spatial frequency if the animal responds by tracking the grating.
Stop increasing the spatial frequency when the animal no longer tracks the stimulus.
Record the maximal spatial frequency threshold as the optokinetic threshold for both eyes.
Remove the animal from the pedestal and return it to its home cage.
Dilate pupils with 1% tropicamide and 2.5% phenylephrine.
Anesthetize eyes with topical 0.5% proparacaine HCl.
Sedate animals with intraperitoneal ketamine/xylazine (100/10 mg/kg).
Keep eyes lubricated with 2.5% Goniovisc Hypromellose.
Use the Micron IV imaging system to capture bright field images of the retina.
Place 0.5% erythromycin ointment on eyes and let animals recover from anesthesia.
Enucleate the eye as rapidly as possible after euthanasia following IACUC guidelines.
Place the enucleated eye into cold 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Maintain a 10–20× fixative to tissue ratio.
Remove the anterior chamber including the lens after 10–60 min of fixation.
Replace the remaining eye cup with fresh 4% PFA.
Place samples in PFA on ice and store at 2°C–8°C for 24–48 h.
Remove the PFA solution and add an equal volume of cold 10% sucrose solution in 1×PBS.
Store the eyes in 2°C–8°C for 24 h.
Replace with an equal volume of cold 20% sucrose solution after removing the 10% sucrose solution.
Place the eyes in 2°C–8°C for another 24 h.
Remove the 20% sucrose solution and replace with an equal volume of cold 30% sucrose solution.
Store the eyes in 2°C–8°C for 24 h.
Remove the eye cup from the 30% sucrose solution and dab dry on a piece of filter paper.
Place the eye cup cut side down on filter paper to allow vitreous drainage until the filter paper remains dry.
Place the eye cup into a labeled cryomold.
Fill the cryomold with OCT media.
Orient the eye cup toward the front of the cryomold.
Position the injection site at 2 o'clock for left eyes and 10 o'clock for right eyes.
Freeze the cryomold in a liquid nitrogen bath, ensuring that the liquid nitrogen does not touch the OCT media directly.
Remove the cryomold from the liquid nitrogen when the OCT media no longer has a glossy shine.
Wrap the cryomold tightly in aluminum foil to limit exposure to air.
Place wrapped blocks in a -20°C freezer.
Section eye blocks at 12 μm.
Obtain approximately 40 slides containing 4 sections per slide from each eye.
Collect sections in a 5-slide series, providing a representative section every 60 μm on each slide throughout the eye cup.
Stain the first slide of each series with cresyl violet or hematoxylin and eosin.
Dry slides for at least 30 min after removing from freezer.
Block for 45 min with 4% horse serum, 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA), and 0.5% triton x in phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Add primary antibodies to blocking buffer and incubate overnight at 4°C.
Wash slides 3 times with 1× PBS for 5 min each.
Add secondary antibodies to blocking buffer and incubate for 45 min in the dark at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Wash slides 3 times with 1× PBS for 5 min each.
Incubate with DAPI in the dark for 10 min.
Wash slides 2 times with 1× PBS for 5 min each.
Coverslip the slides with 100 μL of Fluoromount G.
Quantify photoreceptors by measuring outer nuclear layer thickness (ONL).
Use a scanning laser confocal microscope with LAS AF software to image stained slides.
Set consistent laser intensity settings for each emission wavelength.
Collect Z-stack images at ×10 and ×20 magnification with 1-μm step size.
Save color channel z-stacks as separate TIFF files.
Flatten each color channel z-stack and save the flattened images as TIFF files.
Count ONL cell bodies within rows of the ONL in both temporal (injected) and nasal (non-injected) regions.
Count cone arrestin positive cells in both temporal (injected) and nasal (non-injected) regions.
Generate counts by three observers blinded to dosage and age group.
Average ONL counts and photoreceptor counts per group for data presentation.
